title: Dry shampoo powder
subtitle: A waterless hair refresh for second-day hair
excerpt: Dry shampoo powder is a blend of arrowroot starch, kaolin clay, and bicarbonate of soda that absorbs excess sebum at the roots without water. Sifted onto the scalp and combed through, it revives second-day hair in a few minutes. This formula makes about 50 g of powder; use cocoa powder in place of some arrowroot for dark hair.
sourceNotes: Arrowroot starch as a dry shampoo base: Organic Beauty by Margo Marrone (2013, Ryland Peters & Small). Kaolin clay for oil absorption: The Handmade Apothecary by Kim Walker and Vicky Chown (2017). Bicarbonate of soda: use sparingly as scalp deodoriser, excessive baking soda can disrupt scalp pH (pH ~5.5) and cause dryness with prolonged use. Cocoa powder recommendation for dark hair from the same tradition.

recipe.yieldDescription: ~50 g dry shampoo powder (about 15 to 20 applications)
recipe.batchNotes: Scale up as needed; keep the ratios the same. Store in a shaker jar or salt cellar for easy dispensing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix in a large batch. The powder keeps indefinitely in a sealed jar kept dry.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: One year in a sealed jar at room temperature if kept dry. A small silica gel sachet inside the jar helps prevent clumping in humid bathrooms.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fine white starch extracted from the arrowroot plant, used in cosmetics as a silky, absorbent filler. In dry shampoo it absorbs sebum at the hair roots and reduces the look and feel of greasy hair.

content.text: Dry shampoo powder is a blend of

, kaolin clay, and a small amount of bicarbonate of soda that absorbs excess sebum at the roots without water. Sifted onto the scalp and combed through, it revives second-day hair in a few minutes. Makes about 50 g, roughly fifteen to twenty applications.

For dark hair: replace 10 g of arrowroot with 10 g of cocoa powder, or blend to a shade that matches the hair. The arrowroot base is pale and can leave a white cast on dark hair without the adjustment.

items.prepNote: main absorbent base; replace 10 g with cocoa powder for dark hair
additional oil absorption; white kaolin is fine for all hair colours
scalp deodoriser; keep the proportion low, excessive use disrupts scalp pH
optional fragrance; mix into the powder and let dry fully before sealing

content.text: Combine the arrowroot, kaolin clay, and bicarbonate of soda in a bowl and sift together to remove lumps and aerate the blend. If adding essential oil, drip it in and mix thoroughly with a fork, then leave the powder uncovered for 30 minutes for the oil to disperse before sealing. Pour into a small jar or salt cellar with a shaker top.

Section the hair and shake a small amount of powder onto the roots. Leave for two minutes, then work through with fingertips and comb through from root to tip. The powder absorbs the sebum as it moves through the hair and brushes out cleanly. Start with less than you think you need, it is easier to add more than to brush out excess.
One year in a sealed jar kept dry. If the powder clumps, the jar has taken on moisture, empty it, spread on a tray to dry, and re-sift before sealing again.
